case_number: Civil Appeal Nos. of 2022 (Arising out of SLP (C) Nos. 8658-8659 of 2019 et seq.)

parties.petitioner: The Employees Provident Fund Organisation & Anr.

summary: Challenge to the legality of amendments made by the Central Government to the Employees’ Pension Scheme, 1995 via notification G.S.R. 609(E) dated 22nd August 2014, which increased the pensionable salary ceiling to Rs.15,000 but restricted coverage, particularly for employees in exempted establishments. The judgment examined the validity of capping pensionable salary, abrogation of the proviso to paragraph 11(3) allowing retrospective option for higher pension, and conflicting High Court decisions (Kerala, Delhi, Rajasthan). Central issue: whether employees have a vested right to opt for higher pension benefits regardless of delayed exercise of option. The Court considered precedents including R.C. Gupta v. RPFO and assessed constitutional and statutory obligations under the EPF & MP Act, 1952.
legal_provisions_cited: Section 6A, Employees’ Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952
R.C. Gupta and Others vs. Regional Provident Fund Commissioner, Employees Provident Fund Organisation and Others, (2018) 14 SCC 809
Union of India v. A. Majeed Kunju
final_judgment: The Supreme Court upheld the right of employees to exercise the option for higher pension under the proviso to paragraph 11(3) of the Pension Scheme without time restriction, invalidated the 2014 amendments to the extent they restricted such rights, and confirmed the Kerala, Delhi, and Rajasthan High Courts’ judgments quashing the impugned notifications and circulars.
